headline: A quiet, foggy start gives way to light rain this weekend, then a much stormier, wetter and windier pattern takes over from Tuesday through the rest of the week, with a growing risk of coastal flooding.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Saturday starts cold and foggy, with temperatures in the upper 20s to mid 30s overnight and patches of freezing fog possible this morning, especially over and near the water and in low-lying areas and valleys; low clouds and fog may linger until about 10 AM. High pressure moves inland today as a low-pressure system drops south toward the coast. Light rain reaches the coast this afternoon and spreads into the Puget Sound lowlands and the rest of the interior this evening, with highs in the mid 40s to low 50s.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: The low sits offshore through Sunday, keeping rain light: only a few hundredths of an inch for the interior, including Puget Sound, with many spots staying dry, and a tenth to a quarter inch along the coast. Snow levels stay around 2,000 to 3,000 feet, giving the Cascade passes less than half an inch of snow. On Monday another round of rain and snow moves in but focuses mainly on the Olympic Peninsula, where the Olympic Mountains could pick up 4 to 8 inches of snow. Highs stay in the mid 40s to low 50s through Monday.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A broad storm system strengthens offshore Monday night into Tuesday and sends a series of disturbances across western Washington. Expect multiple rounds of widespread lowland rain, mountain snow and gusty winds starting Tuesday and continuing through the second half of the week. Rivers will rise; widespread river flooding isn't expected, but the Skokomish River will likely reach flood stage late in the week.

coast: High tides this weekend could bring minor coastal flooding to the Pacific Coast and the Strait of Juan de Fuca by Sunday, and next week's storms plus high tides raise the coastal flooding threat further, most notably on the Pacific Coast, where Tuesday's storm also brings another round of high surf. On the water, a Gale Warning runs until 4 PM Saturday for the outer coastal waters (10–60 miles out) from Cape Flattery to James Island, followed there by a Small Craft Advisory until 4 AM Sunday; Small Craft Advisories also cover the rest of the coastal waters until 4 AM Sunday, the western and central Strait of Juan de Fuca from 4 AM to 4 PM Saturday, and the eastern Strait (off Port Angeles and Sequim) from 1 PM Saturday to 4 AM Sunday. Winds of 20–30 knots hit the coastal waters and eastern Strait today, staying gusty from the southeast Sunday into Monday, and a couple of strong storms Monday into Tuesday and again Wednesday bring a high chance of gale-force gusts on the coastal waters and part of the eastern Strait, plus a 20–40% chance of storm-force gusts. Seas build from 6–8 feet to 8–12 feet today and to 16–20 feet Monday, easing to 10–14 feet by the end of the week; patchy fog is possible on the inland waters this morning, and no thunderstorms are expected this weekend.
watch_for: Freezing fog this morning in low-lying areas and near the water.
The stormy stretch starting Tuesday: repeated rounds of rain, mountain snow and gusty winds, with possible storm-force gusts on the water.
Coastal flooding with high tides from Sunday into next week, and the Skokomish River likely reaching flood stage late in the week.
confidence: Forecasters sound settled on light weekend rain and on next week turning stormier, with high odds of gales on the water, but they give no rain, snow or wind amounts yet for Tuesday onward.
